rag.description: Read a single value from SQL Server, such as a row count, a total, or a status, and reuse it in later automation steps. Typed query parameters keep input out of the SQL text, stored credentials or connection strings select the database, and consistent text output keeps comparisons and branching reliable.

qa.question: What does the GetSqlServerScalar plugin do?
qa.answer: It runs a SQL query on SQL Server and stores the first column of the first row as a single value.

qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of GetSqlServerScalar?
qa.answer: CommandText or CommandFile holds the query, the Base64 switch decodes a Base64-encoded CommandText, Parameters supplies JSON values for @ placeholders, and CommandTimeout limits run time. The result is stored as GetSqlServerScalar:Value.

qa.question: How does GetSqlServerScalar fit into an automation workflow?
qa.answer: It runs as an Action task step with the database icon and the ActionRuleModel, and its value feeds conditions, assertions, or later steps.

qa.question: What are best practices for using GetSqlServerScalar?
qa.answer: Pass every input through Parameters instead of building SQL text, and use CommandFile or a Base64-encoded CommandText with the Base64 switch for SQL that contains ` --` or `}}`.

qa.question: How does GetSqlServerScalar run inline SQL that contains ` --` or `}}`?
qa.answer: Encode the SQL as UTF-8 Base64, pass it as CommandText, and add the Base64 switch, or put the SQL in a CommandFile. Only CommandText is decoded, so CommandFile content is read as plain text and the Parameters JSON stays plain.

qa.question: How is a GetSqlServerScalar rule configured?
qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “GetSqlServerScalar” and an argument such as {{$ --Credentials:sql-production --CommandText:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.Orders WHERE Status = @Status --Parameters:{"Status":"Open"} --CommandTimeout:60}}.

Connects with a stored credentials name, a connection string, or discrete server settings, and stores the value as a session parameter for later steps.

qa.question: Where are the GetSqlServerScalar documentation and source code?
qa.answer: It is documented as a single-value SQL Server query step. Documentation: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/docs/Actions/GetSqlServerScalar.md. Source: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/src/G4.Plugins.SqlServer/Actions/GetSqlServerScalar.cs.

qa.question: How does GetSqlServerScalar handle errors and empty results?
qa.answer: A query that returns no row or NULL stores an empty value, while SQL errors, timeouts, a missing query, a CommandText that is not valid Base64 while the Base64 switch is set, or invalid Parameters JSON fail the step.

description: ### Purpose
Runs a SQL Server query and returns a single value from the first column of the first row.
Gives automations a quick way to read counts, totals, flags, or lookup values without exporting a full result set.
Keeps input safe by sending values as typed SQL parameters instead of joining them into the query.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature                    | Description                                                                                                                                 |
| Single-value query         | Returns the first column of the first row, such as the result of `SELECT COUNT(*)`.                                                         |
| Inline or file query       | Reads the query from CommandText, a Base64-encoded CommandText with the Base64 switch, or a UTF-8 `.sql` file in CommandFile.               |
| Typed parameters           | Binds JSON object properties to `@` placeholders as typed SQL parameters.                                                                   |
| Consistent value text      | Stores strings as they are and other types as JSON text, such as `42`, `true`, or `2024-01-01T00:00:00`.                                    |
| Empty result handling      | Stores an empty value when the query returns no row or NULL.                                                                                |
| Flexible connection input  | Resolves the target from a credentials name or id, a raw connection string, or discrete server, database, and sign-in settings.             |
| Command timeout            | Limits query run time in seconds, with a default of 30 seconds and 0 for no limit.                                                          |
| Session and entity outputs | Stores the value as the Base64 session parameter `GetSqlServerScalar:Value` and returns it in the response entity unless `NoEntity` is set. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case          | Description                                                                           |
| Work queue sizing | Count open orders or pending requests to decide how much work a bot should take.      |
| Lookup values     | Read a customer id, price, or status by key and reuse it in later form-filling steps. |
| Run guards        | Read the last processed date or a control flag before a job starts.                   |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case               | Description                                                                      |
| Back-end verification  | Confirm that a UI action wrote the expected row count or status to the database. |
| Test data checks       | Verify that seed data exists before a test suite runs.                           |
| Before and after delta | Compare a count before and after a test step to prove one record was added.      |
### Notes
Use CommandFile, or encode CommandText as UTF-8 Base64 and add the Base64 switch, for SQL that contains ` --` or `}}`, because those sequences end an inline argument value.
The value is plain text in the response entity and Base64-encoded in the session parameter.
Stores the first column of the first row returned by the query.
Strings are stored as they are, other types as JSON text such as `42`, `true`, or `2024-01-01T00:00:00`, and a NULL value or an empty result is stored as an empty value.
Returned as plain text in the response entity for direct data transfer.

annotations.expected_result: The step stores the number of open orders, such as `42`, in `GetSqlServerScalar:Value` and returns it in the response entity.
annotations.notes: The stored credentials record selects the server and login, and the `Status` value is sent as a typed SQL parameter instead of being joined into the query. The query may run for up to 60 seconds.

description: ### Count open orders with a parameterized query
The argument binds the `sql-production` credentials, a `SELECT COUNT(*)` query, and the JSON parameters `{"Status":"Open"}` at runtime.
The `@Status` placeholder receives `Open` as a typed value, and the count becomes the stored value.

edge_cases: Orders table is empty, so the value is empty
Windows identity has no access to the database
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the latest order date, such as `2024-01-01T00:00:00`, in `GetSqlServerScalar:Value` and returns no response entity.
annotations.notes: The raw connection string is used because no Credentials value is set. A date result is stored as ISO 8601 text, and the `NoEntity` switch keeps the value only in the session parameter.

description: ### Read the latest order date from a connection string
The argument binds a full connection string, a parameterless `SELECT MAX(OrderDate)` query, and the `NoEntity` switch.
The step stores the value only as a session parameter.

edge_cases: Database override is not accessible to the stored login
Query in the file returns NULL
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the stock level for `SKU-1042` in `GetSqlServerScalar:Value` and returns it in the response entity.
annotations.notes: The stored credentials record supplies the login, and the `Database` parameter switches the connection to `Inventory`. The query text comes from a `.sql` file, which safely holds comments and braces that would end a plain inline argument and is read without Base64 decoding.

description: ### Read a stock level from a SQL file
The argument binds the `sql-production` credentials, the `Inventory` database, the JSON parameters `{"Sku":"SKU-1042"}`, and the `C:\Sql\stock-level.sql` file.
The query in the file uses the `@Sku` placeholder, and its first value becomes the stored value.

edge_cases: Base64 switch is absent, so the encoded text is sent as SQL and the step fails
CommandText is not valid Base64, so the step fails before connecting
No order is open, so the stored value is `0`
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the number of open orders, such as `42`, in `GetSqlServerScalar:Value` and returns it in the response entity.
annotations.notes: The Base64 switch decodes CommandText from UTF-8 Base64 before the query runs, so the ` --` comment travels inline without ending the argument value. A `COUNT(*)` query always returns one row, so the value is a number even when no order matches.

description: ### Count open orders with a Base64-encoded query
The argument binds the `sql-production` credentials, a Base64 CommandText, and the Base64 switch at runtime.
The decoded SQL is `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.Orders -- open orders only` followed by a `WHERE Status = 'Open'` line, and the count becomes the stored value.
Stores the first column of the first row returned by the query.
Strings are stored as they are, other types as JSON text such as `42`, `true`, or `2024-01-01T00:00:00`, and a NULL value or an empty result is stored as an empty value.
Lets later steps reuse a count, total, or lookup value without running another query.
The session value is Base64-encoded, so decode it before use.

description: Selects how the connection signs in to SQL Server, such as a SQL login, the Windows identity, or a Microsoft Entra method.
Overrides the authentication method from the credentials or the connection string for this step only.
Choosing the right method avoids login failures on servers that accept only certain sign-in types.
parameters.name: Authentication

description: Signs in with a SQL Server login name and password.
Use it together with the Username and Password parameters.
values.name: Sql Password

description: Signs in with the Windows identity of the account that runs the automation.
No user name or password is sent with the connection.
values.name: Integrated

description: Signs in with the first available Microsoft Entra identity on the machine, such as a managed identity or developer tool sign-in.
Suits automation that moves between local machines and cloud hosts.
values.name: Active Directory Default

description: Signs in with the Microsoft Entra identity of the signed-in Windows user.
Works on domain-joined or Entra-joined machines without a password.
values.name: Active Directory Integrated

description: Opens a Microsoft Entra sign-in prompt for the user.
Fits attended runs where a person can complete the sign-in, including multi-factor prompts.
values.name: Active Directory Interactive

description: Signs in with the managed identity of the Azure resource that runs the automation.
Keeps stored secrets out of cloud-hosted runs.
values.name: Active Directory Managed Identity

description: Signs in with a Microsoft Entra user name and password.
Use it together with the Username and Password parameters.
values.name: Active Directory Password

description: Signs in as a Microsoft Entra application.
Pass the application id as Username and the client secret as Password.
values.name: Active Directory Service Principal

description: Decodes the CommandText value from UTF-8 Base64 before the query runs.
Encoding the SQL as Base64 lets inline text that contains a space followed by two dashes or a double closing brace travel safely, because those sequences otherwise end an inline argument value.
Only CommandText is decoded, so CommandFile content is always read as plain text and the Parameters JSON stays plain.
Invalid Base64 fails the step before anything is sent to SQL Server, so encoded text never runs as SQL.
parameters.name: Base64

description: Points to a UTF-8 `.sql` file that holds the query, such as `C:\Sql\stock-level.sql`.
Applies when CommandText is empty, and the step fails when the file does not exist.
Lets queries that contain comments or braces run without breaking the inline argument.
parameters.name: CommandFile

description: Holds the SQL query to run, such as `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.Orders WHERE Status = @Status`.
Takes priority over CommandFile, and the step fails when neither one is set.
When the SQL contains ` --` or `}}`, use CommandFile or pass the text as UTF-8 Base64 with the Base64 switch, because those sequences end an inline argument value.
parameters.name: CommandText

description: Sets how many seconds the query may run before the step fails with a timeout error, with a default of 30 seconds.
A value of 0 waits without a time limit, and an invalid or negative value falls back to the default.
parameters.name: CommandTimeout

description: Supplies a full ADO.NET connection string, such as `Server=localhost,1433;Database=Sales;Integrated Security=True;TrustServerCertificate=True`.
Applies only when Credentials is not set, so a stored credentials reference always takes priority.
Discrete parameters such as Server or Database still override the matching parts of the string.
parameters.name: ConnectionString

description: Names a stored SQL Server credentials record by name or id, such as `sql-production`, so secrets stay out of the rule.
When no record matches, a value that contains `=` is used as a raw connection string and any other value is used as a raw Microsoft Entra access token.
Takes priority over ConnectionString, while discrete parameters such as Database still override the resolved values.
parameters.name: Credentials

description: Sets the database the connection opens in, such as `Sales`.
Overrides the database from the credentials or connection string, so one stored login can reach several databases.
parameters.name: Database

description: Sets the transport encryption mode of the connection.
Overrides the encryption setting from the credentials or connection string when a server requires a specific mode.
parameters.name: Encrypt

description: Requires an encrypted connection and validates the server certificate unless TrustServerCertificate is set.
Fits most production servers.
values.name: Mandatory

description: Encrypts the connection only when the server requires it.
Suits local development servers without a trusted certificate.
values.name: Optional

description: Encrypts the connection before login and always validates the server certificate.
Requires a server that supports TDS 8.0, such as SQL Server 2022 or Azure SQL Database.
values.name: Strict

description: Omits the response entity, so the outputs are stored only as session parameters.
Keeps responses small when later steps read only the session parameters.
parameters.name: NoEntity

description: Supplies query parameter values as a JSON object, such as `{"Status":"Open"}`, where each property binds to the matching `@` placeholder.
Values are sent as typed SQL parameters and never joined into the query text, which protects against SQL injection.
Strings, booleans, numbers, and null keep their type, while nested objects and arrays are sent as JSON text.
The `@` prefix is added automatically when a property name omits it.
parameters.name: Parameters

description: Sets the password used with the Username login.
Overrides the password from the credentials or connection string for this step.
Prefer Credentials over a plain password so secrets are not stored in the rule.
parameters.name: Password

description: Sets the TCP port of the server, such as `1433`, and joins it to Server as `server,port`.
Applies only when Server is set in the same step, because the port is combined with that server name.
parameters.name: Port

description: Sets the SQL Server host name or address, such as `localhost` or `db01\SQLEXPRESS`.
Overrides the server from the credentials or connection string.
The step fails when no server is resolved from Credentials, ConnectionString, or Server.
parameters.name: Server

description: Supplies a raw Microsoft Entra access token that signs in the connection.
Enables token sign-in without a stored password.
Do not combine it with Password or Authentication, because the SQL Server client rejects that mix when the connection opens.
parameters.name: Token

description: Accepts the server certificate without validating it against a trusted authority.
Helps connect to development servers that use a self-signed certificate.
Avoid it in production, because it removes protection against a spoofed server.
parameters.name: TrustServerCertificate

description: Sets the login name used with Password, such as a SQL login or a Microsoft Entra user or application id.
Overrides the user name from the credentials or connection string for this step.
parameters.name: Username
